Title: Spontaneous motility in preterm, small-for-gestational age infants. I. Quantitative aspects.
Journal: Early human development
Outcome: spontaneous motility
Evidence_Quote: The developmental course of the quantitative aspects of early spontaneous motility was studied longitudinally in fourteen intrauterine growth-retarded infants, with a birth weight below the 5th percentile

Title: Spontaneous motility in preterm, small-for-gestational age infants. II. Qualitative aspects.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: preterm infants with a birth weight below the 5th percentile
Outcome: quality of general movements (GMs); neurological outcome at 24 months
Evidence_Quote: The quality of general movements (GMs) was studied longitudinally during the preterm and postterm period until approximately 20 weeks corrected age, using Prechtl's method of quality assessment.

Title: Decreased cardiac responses to auditory stimulation during prone sleep.
Journal: Pediatrics
Target_Age: healthy infants, median age 11 weeks (30 studied, 20 analyzed)
Outcome: auditory challenge induces smaller cardiac responses in prone than in supine sleep
Evidence_Quote: Their behavioral and cardiac responses were recorded during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, both before and after exposure to 90 dB (A) of white-noise.

Title: A cross-language comparison of vowel perception in English-learning and German-learning infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants in two age groups (6-8 months and 10-12 months)
Outcome: vowel discrimination
Evidence_Quote: discrimination of /dut/ versus /dyt/ and /d epsilon t/ versus /daet/ was examined in English- and German-learning infants in two age groups (6-8 months and 10-12 months) using the conditioned headturn procedure

Title: The perceptual magnet effect as an emergent property of neural map formation.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: perceptual magnet effect; perceptual space warping
Evidence_Quote: The perceptual magnet effect is one of the earliest known language-specific phenomena arising in infant speech development.

Title: Speech perception is hearing sounds, not tongues.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: speech perception; differentiation of sound contrasts
Evidence_Quote: Infants and various nonhuman species can differentiate certain sound contrasts in human speech

Title: Anatomical correlates of the passive properties underlying the developmental shift in the frequency map of the mammalian cochlea.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: basilar membrane dimensions do not change as the place code shifts; organ of Corti size and basilar membrane fiber-band thickness do
Evidence_Quote: regions that code for the roughly the same frequency (e.g., approximately 11.2 kHz) at different ages can have basilar membranes of very different dimensions

Title: Infant vocalizations in response to speech: vocal imitation and developmental change.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants at 12, 16, and 20 weeks of age
Outcome: infant vocalizations; vocal imitation
Evidence_Quote: examine developmental change in infants' vocalizations in response to adults' vowels at 12, 16, and 20 weeks of age and test for vocal imitation

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning curves in human adults and neonates.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 15 normal-hearing adults and 16 healthy term-born neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with suppressor tone (iso-suppression tuning curves)
Outcome: DPOAE STCs stable with tip centered at f2; neonatal STCs at 3000 and 6000 Hz comparable to adults, suggesting mature cochlear tuning by term birth
Evidence_Quote: The 2f1-f2 DPOAE was elicited using f2/f1 = 1.2, LI = 1.2, LI = 65 and L2 = 50 dB SPL. A suppressor tone was presented at frequencies ranging from 1 octave below to 1/4 octave above f2 and varied in level until DPOAE amplitude was reduced by 6 dB. The suppressor level required for 6 dB suppression was plotted as function of suppressor frequency to generate a DPOAE STC. Forward-masked psychoacoustic tuning curves (PTC) were obtained for three of the adult subjects. Results indicate that DPOAE STCs are stable and show minimal inter- and intra-subject variability. The tip of the STC is consistently centered around the f2 region and STCs are similar in shape, width (Q10) and slope to VIIIth-nerve TCs. PTCs and STCs measured in the same subject showed similar trends, although PTCs had narrower width and steeper slope. Neonatal STCs were recorded at 3000 and 6000 Hz only

Title: Sensory consonance and the perceptual similarity of complex-tone harmonic intervals: tests of adult and infant listeners.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: perceptual similarity; discrimination
Evidence_Quote: 7-month-old infants were tested with an operant headturn procedure in a similar design and exhibited an identical pattern of responding

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) amplitude as a function of f2/f1 frequency ratio and primary tone level separation in human adults and neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2/f1 ratio and primary level separation varied)
Outcome: optimal f2/f1 ratio comparable in adults and neonates; 10-15 dB level separation optimal in adults and term neonates but not premature neonates
Evidence_Quote: Two f2 frequencies were investigated: 1500 and 6000 Hz.

Title: On the heritability of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions: A twins study.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: human monozygotic and dizygotic twins; non-twins
Outcome: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions
Evidence_Quote: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) were measured in human monozygotic (MZ) and dizygotic (DZ) twins and in a sample of non-twins.

Title: Infants' pitch perception: inharmonic tonal complexes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic and inharmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental)
Outcome: infants discriminate and categorize inharmonic complexes by pitch; performance deteriorates for the more strongly inharmonic complexes (30 Hz partial shift)
Evidence_Quote: infants demonstrated the ability to discriminate two harmonic complexes based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: Filtering and spectral characteristics of averaged auditory brain-stem response and background noise in infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts (ABR); 30-Hz vs 100-Hz high-pass recording filters
Outcome: infant ABR energy concentrated below 100 Hz; 30 Hz high-pass filter yields larger-amplitude ABR and better signal-to-noise ratio than 100 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli used to elicit ABRs are moderate- and low-level clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts.

Title: Gap detection in infants, children, and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: gap-detection thresholds ~11 ms (infants), 5.6 ms (children), 5.2 ms (adults)
Evidence_Quote: Listeners who were 6.5 months, 12 months, 5 years, and 21 years of age were required to discriminate a pair of 500-Hz, Gaussian-enveloped tone pips from a short 500-Hz tone of the same duration and total energy.

Title: Infants require low-frequency energy to hear the pitch of the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental) with low- or high-frequency energy
Outcome: infants categorize low-frequency (resolvable) complexes by missing-fundamental pitch but fail to categorize high-frequency (unresolvable) complexes
Evidence_Quote: infants first learned to discriminate two harmonic tonal complexes based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: Infant psychometric functions for detection: mechanisms of immature sensitivity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: auditory detection; psychometric functions
Evidence_Quote: Psychometric functions are described for individual 6- to 9-month-old infants and for individual adults for auditory detection of repeated, long- and short-duration tone bursts in quiet

Title: Development of cochlear potentials in the neonatal gerbil.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: auditory nerve compound action potentials; cochlear microphonics; endocochlear potential
Evidence_Quote: Auditory nerve compound action potentials (CAP) and cochlear microphonics (CM) were measured at the round window, and the endocochlear potential (EP) was recorded at three different locations in pups aged 13 to 30 days after birth (DAB) and in 90 day-old animals.

Title: The development of frequency resolution in humans as revealed by the auditory brain-stem response recorded with notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: 3-month-olds do not have adultlike tuning for 8000 Hz stimulation; tuning-function width is adultlike by 6 months for high- and low-frequency probes
Evidence_Quote: Tone-pip stimuli at 1000, 4000, and 8000 Hz (50 dB nHL) were presented simultaneously with notched-noise masking

Title: Frequency contribution to the click-evoked auditory brain-stem response in human adults and infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: infants show adultlike latency shifts across notch center frequencies, suggesting mature tonotopic organization by 3 months
Evidence_Quote: when the ABR is recorded in the presence of notched-noise masking with center frequencies ranging from 500-8000 Hz

Title: Intrinsic F0 of vowels in the babbling of 6-, 9-, and 12-month-old French- and English-learning infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: intrinsic F0 of vowels
Evidence_Quote: It is found, instead, that IF0 appears even in babbling.
